newsitem.title: NEPAL: China's Jiang asks Nepal to eye Tibetan market.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang asks Nepal to eye Tibetan market.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin has urged Nepal to produce more marketable goods for export to Tibet as a means of trimming a lopsided trade imbalance with its giant northern neighbour.

"We hope that Nepal will produce more marketable products to increase its exports to Tibet," Jiang, set to arrive in the Himalayan kingdom later on Wednesday, was quoted by Nepal's official RSS news agency as saying.

In the 12 months to mid-July 1995, Nepal exported $4.7 million worth of goods to China and imported $57.6 million worth. The $52.9 million trade shortfall was 21 percent greater than during the previous 12-month period.
Currently Nepal's exports to China consist mainly of animal and vegetable oil, fat, biscuits, bread and tobacco. Nepali businessmen are keen to sell bricks, wrought iron and cement.
Most trade is on a barter basis, and commerce between Nepal and neighbouring Tibet is negligible.
Jiang was scheduled to arrive in Nepal from Pakistan on the last leg of a South Asian tour which also took him to India. He was set to depart the Nepal capital Kathmandu on Thursday.
Jiang said Beijing was ready to gradually reduce its trade imbalance with Nepal while vigorously expanding two-way trade.
"We both should make full use of the existing trade channel to expand the two-way trade and cooperation," RSS quoted Jiang as saying.
Nepal, often described as a yam between two boulders, strives to balance its relations between its giant neighbours, China to the north and India to the south.
Kathmandu recognises Beijing's sovereignty over Tibet and bows to China's sensitivities over Taiwan.
Jiang said relations between China and Nepal set an example in carrying out five principles of peaceful co-existence.
"China always maintains that all countries, big or small, rich or poor, strong or weak, are equal members of the international community," the Chinese president said.
Nepali officials said an economic cooperation agreement was expected to be signed later on Wednesday after Jiang and King Birendra hold brief talks.
